2002-GR-11.6.3-1.not-in-2014: normalized text not found in specs/ISO_COBOL_2014.md

read.suite-runs-at-2002: I compiled and ran these at --std 2002 with the pinned compiler, and each matched its .out: pb894_program_prototype_2002, pb988_end_markers, pb1505_final_method_through_intermediates, pb759_parameterized_class, oo_implements_repeated, pb1502_interface_inherits_legal, l1p5_interface_inherits_multiple, oo_property_methods, oo_override_final, oo_hello, literal_concat, and l1c08_end_marker_closes_unit (at 85 and at 2002). Each of these refusal tests gave its expected diagnostic at --std 2002: pb1391-abbrev-* (4), pb894-program-prototype-signature, l1c09-factory-implements-nonconforming-method, pb1502-interface-inherits-conflicting-prototypes, l1m7-method-prototype-override, l1c18-method-prototype-final, oo-inherits-same-base-twice, pb988-end-* (7). The programs were run from E:/COBOL/conformance-suite and their outputs are under probes-q-06/suite/.

defects.summary: At --std 2002, the compiler refuses multiple class inheritance (an INHERITS clause of CLASS-ID that names two or more distinct classes) with COBOL0849. The diagnostic cites the 2023 optional-element licence (§2023:4.2.7, Annex A.4.10 item 1). The 2002 standard has no such licence. Its 3.1 makes only Annex A, the communications facility, optional, and B.3 lists no OO item. 2002 11.2.1 admits { class-name-2 } ..., and 9.3.9 says a subclass inherits from one or more classes.
defects.program: probes-q-06/mi/diamond.cob: Q6DA defines M1 FINAL; Q6DB and Q6DC each INHERIT FROM Q6DA; Q6DD INHERITS FROM Q6DB Q6DC; the main program invokes D "M1". Also probes-q-06/mi/mi_override.cob (Q6MD INHERITS FROM Q6MB Q6MC with METHOD-ID. MB OVERRIDE).
defects.expected: Accepted. The program runs and prints A-M1-FINAL. §2002:11.2.2 SR6: 'If the same method is inherited from one superclass through two or more intermediate superclasses, it may be specified with the FINAL clause' (OK). §2002:9.3.9: 'inherits from one or more classes, known as superclasses' (OK). §2002:3.1: 'shall provide the normative elements specified in 6, Reference format through 16, Standard classes' (OK).
defects.observed: diamond.cob(47,42): error COBOL0849: class 'Q6DD': INHERITS FROM 2 base classes (Q6DB, Q6DC): Multiple inheritance ... is an OPTIONAL element (§2023:4.2.7; Annex A.4.10 item 1) whose support WiseOwl COBOL does not claim ... exit 65. The same refusal occurs at --std 2023, where it is licensed. mi_override.cob gives the same COBOL0849.

So in 2002 both sentences govern multiple-inheritance classes, and the compiler refuses every such class at --std 2002. That refusal is a compiler defect (D1). This is a fifth cause: the edition's optional-feature licence differs.
